Meanwhile, every database faces a hard limit: disks are slow, memory is fast. A cache stores hot rows near the query path, so repeated reads skip costly lookups and return in microseconds rather than tens of milliseconds under heavy load.

However, correctness now becomes the real problem; a stale cache can serve data that no longer exists. Teams pick invalidation strategies carefully: write-through updates the cache during each write; read-through fills it lazily on a miss. Time-based expiry helps too, though tuning that window demands real traffic data from production systems and patient, careful measurement.

Along with sizing, monitor hit ratios daily; a low ratio hints at poor locality, or at a RAM pool too small for actual traffic. Add shards, adjust hash rings, and warm hot data during rollouts, avoiding origin storms.

Finally, treat cache design as an ongoing craft, measuring, tuning, and pruning cache keys until the real work reads done.
